topic.title: Working with assessment evidence
topic.description: A short authoring example with fictional evidence.

activities.title: From observation to conclusion
activities.description: Learn to state the limits of an observation.

content.markdown: An **observation** records what you saw. A conclusion explains what the observation supports.

content.objective: Write an observation and a limited conclusion.
content.safety: Use only the fictional example provided.

steps.title: Record what the evidence shows
steps.instructions: A fictional booking export has a blank date field. Record the observation before suggesting what to check next.
steps.expectedResult: A sentence identifying the missing value and one follow-up question.
steps.hint: Describe what you can see before suggesting why the field is blank.
steps.workedAnswer: The exported record has no booking date. Does the source booking record contain a date?

activities.title: Assess a fictional record

content.scenario: A fictional retailer presents one weekly stock report with no reviewer listed.
tasks: Separate the observation from your conclusion.

activities.solution: The supplied report does not identify a reviewer. Ask for review records before concluding that reviews never happen.

summary: State what the evidence shows and note what you cannot conclude from it.

roles.title: Inventory manager
actions: Assign a person to review the weekly report and agree when the review is due.

roles.title: Operations team
actions: Record who reviewed the report and when. Retrieve a report from an earlier week to check that the record is available.

assurance: Request evidence from more than one week before making a finding about how often reviews happen.

questions.question: A single report has no reviewer listed. What does that support?

options.label: This report does not identify a reviewer.
No report has ever been reviewed.

questions.explanation: Evidence from one report does not establish what happens across all reports.
